lines.L01: Reference ranges in a PDF. Formulas in a chat. A calculator in another app.
lines.L02: Laboratory knowledge, scattered — and rarely in your own language.
lines.L03: LabGuide brings it together: a laboratory reference and learning app in Uzbek, Russian and English.
lines.L04: Core content works offline and without an account — with no ads and no tracking.
lines.L05: Choose your role, and the home screen follows.
lines.L06: For the laboratory specialist: answers at the bench.
lines.L07: Test cards give units, guideline thresholds and what high or low results can mean — with the source behind each claim.
lines.L08: Calculators work only from your own values, and show the formula, limits and sources.
lines.L09: Quality control: Levey–Jennings charts, with Westgard rules applied to every run.
lines.L10: Record a calibration. Count a differential, with percentages and absolute counts.
lines.L11: Browse the instrument catalog and the atlases.
lines.L12: Specialists can also practise for the qualification category assessment.
lines.L13: And your records stay on your phone.
lines.L14: For the teacher: lecture slides and practical protocols, ready for a big screen — offline too.
lines.L15: Open a class: students join with a QR code or a short code.
lines.L16: Set a lecture test — questions can differ per student.
lines.L17: Then see the results by student, and the hardest questions.
lines.L18: For the student: learn from slides, topic by topic, then check yourself.
lines.L19: Five new questions every day, and topic quizzes where every answer is explained.
lines.L20: Timed practice exams work offline, and mistakes can be practised again.
lines.L21: When your teacher sets a test, it waits on your home screen.
lines.L22: One app for specialist, teacher and student.
lines.L23: LabGuide. A reference and learning aid — it does not diagnose.
